extracted.intended_audience: researchers and readers interested in research integrity, journal editors, and biomedical scientists
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for evaluating the integrity, animal-welfare compliance, and post-publication handling (correction/retraction) of a biomedical animal-study paper. Focuses on data availability, humane endpoints, IACUC compliance, and editorial/policy processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate reporting of tumor sizes and underlying data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns were raised about the mouse tumor sizes reported in Figure 2 (e.g., tumour sizes of up to 5500 Photons/cm2/sec/steradian with SE ~1500; up to 23 cm3 with SE ~6 cm3). The journal asked the corresponding author to provide the individual-level data underlying these results and information about humane endpoints and health monitoring during the tumour experiments. In response, the corresponding author stated that they no longer have access to the data or the requested information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must be able to provide underlying, individual-level data and documentation on request to allow verification of reported measurements; inability to produce these data undermines confidence and can trigger correction or retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humane endpoints and animal health monitoring must meet applicable standards
rubrics_metrics.description: An expert assessed that weekly monitoring of tumour volume as reported in the article would not have met U.S. standards for mouse tumour studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Animal studies must employ monitoring schedules and humane endpoints consistent with accepted national/institutional standards; inadequate monitoring frequency or ill-defined humane endpoints are grounds for concern and possible editorial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the approved IACUC protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative of the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) at MD Anderson reviewed the paper against the animal research protocol approved in 2009 and stated that what is reported in the article is not in compliance with the approved IACUC protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported methods and conduct must match the approved IACUC (or equivalent) protocol; deviations from approved protocols, when confirmed by the institution, can justify retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the journal's Animal Research Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE Editors concluded that the study did not comply with the journal’s Animal Research Policy and therefore retracted the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals enforce their stated animal-research policies; confirmed noncompliance with those policies is a valid reason for retraction even years after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external expert assessment for methodological and welfare concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS ONE Editors consulted an expert in animal welfare and animal research methodology who assessed the article and its monitoring/reporting practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should seek independent expert review of animal welfare and methodology concerns raised post-publication to inform corrective/editorial actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight of institutional review findings and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The IACUC reviewed the paper and recommended retraction based on noncompliance with the approved protocol; editors acted in light of the IACUC recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional findings and recommendations (e.g., from IACUC) carry substantial weight in editorial decisions about corrections or retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication follow-up procedures and COPE-aligned processes
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS stated: 'we follow up in accordance with COPE guidance and PLOS policies as for any other publication ethics case and take additional editorial action when warranted.' Their internal processes for addressing post-publication concerns have evolved; Publication Ethics team formed in 2018.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should have clear, COPE-aligned post-publication investigation procedures; such processes can lead from correction to retraction if new issues are identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections do not preclude later retraction if further issues emerge
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper was corrected in 2012 but later investigated and retracted in 2022 after additional concerns were raised about animal tumour sizes and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A previously issued Correction does not prevent further editorial action; subsequent independent concerns can prompt a re-investigation and possible retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsiveness and engagement with investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Several coauthors 'did not respond or could not be reached.' The corresponding author did not provide requested data and 'did not respond to the retraction decision.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to engage with post-publication inquiries and provide requested materials; lack of cooperation or inability to supply information is a negative factor in resolving concerns and may influence retraction decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate interpretation of tumour measurement standards by context (orthotopic vs subcutaneous)
rubrics_metrics.description: The expert noted that since these tumours are implanted orthotopically and not subcutaneously, typical tumour size limits for subcutaneous humane endpoints do not apply, but nonetheless weekly monitoring reported would not meet U.S. standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations must consider biological/contextual differences (e.g., orthotopic vs subcutaneous implants) but still ensure monitoring and endpoints meet welfare/ethical standards appropriate for the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence of citations after correction and implications for the literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The corrected paper has received 50 citations according to Web of Science, all of which came after the correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections may not stop downstream citation or influence; editors and readers should be aware that corrected (and even later-retracted) papers can continue to shape literature, underscoring the need for clear notices and robust post-publication actions.
